chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan al-Taflīsī, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a dead person and a junub person who are together, while with them there is only enough water for one of them. Which of them should be washed? He said: When a sunnah (prophetic practice) and an obligation come together, the obligation is begun with first.

key_terms.بُدِئَ بِالْفَرْضِ: the obligation is given priority and begun with first
key_terms.جُنُبٍ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a sunnah act, here meaning a non-obligatory prescribed practice
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory duty that takes precedence
key_terms.مَيِّتٍ: a deceased person requiring the ritual washing of the dead

ai.seo_question: If there is only enough water for one ghusl, should it be used for the dead person or for the junub person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about prioritization when available water is sufficient for only one ghusl. The Imam عليه السلام states that when a sunnah (prophetic practice) and a faridah (obligation) coincide, precedence is given to the obligation.
